abstract: <jats:p>Advancing Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF), particularly Fast Ignition and Shock Ignition, requires a deeper understanding of laser–plasma interactions in extreme regimes that remain difficult to access at large-scale ICF facilities. Long-wave infrared (LWIR) lasers provide a powerful approach, leveraging favorable wavelength scaling to access relativistic plasma physics, enable efficient laser beam channeling, and enhance the generation of hot electrons and energetic ions at significantly reduced laser intensity and plasma density. This capability allows laboratory-scale experiments to reproduce ICF-relevant conditions with improved diagnostic access and greater physical transparency. The Brookhaven National Laboratory Accelerator Test Facility offers a unique platform for such studies, combining a multi-terawatt LWIR laser with synchronized optical diagnostics and accelerator-based probes. This capability enables systematic investigation and optimization of key plasma processes governing ICF performance, thereby supporting the development of practical fusion energy systems.</jats:p>
title: Long wave infrared laser platform for plasma studies relevant to inertial fusion

abstract: <jats:p>Configuring a diagnostic before the next shot is an instrumentation problem that grows in importance as high-repetition-rate laser-plasma platforms scale from tens of shots to thousands. In the present campaign, a gated intensified optical camera required shot-to-shot retuning as peak image brightness varied with chamber pressure, laser energy, focus conditions, and target state. Static settings produced under-exposed or over-driven images, while manual tuning consumed shots and reduced measurement efficiency. We treat this problem as machine-learning-guided pre-shot diagnostic configuration using a hybrid framework: archived images and machine variables are reduced to a compact descriptor state, a neural-network surrogate is trained to predict that state from operating conditions and detector settings, and Bayesian optimization inverts the surrogate to recommend executable settings before each shot. On a 1 Hz multi-joule platform, the measured peak signal tracked requested targets from 1000 to 4500 counts with a correlation of 0.92 and a mean absolute error of 15%. These results demonstrate that campaign data can train practical empirical models supporting pre-shot diagnostic configuration for enhanced data quality and experimental efficiency in comparable laser-plasma campaigns.</jats:p>
title: Machine-learning-guided pre-shot diagnostic configuration for high-repetition-rate laser-plasma experiments
